identity.controller: NRage; stick range 100; pad dead zone 5; real N64 range enabled
identity.measurement: External read-only ReadProcessMemory scalar sampler; no RAM writes during capture

preparation.route: Loaded the verified issue35 courtyard baseline in the isolated Project64 clone, navigated the basement to the Lethal Lava Land painting, and entered course 7 through normal gameplay.
preparation.fixture: At the basement key door only, a one-byte Project64 access code wrote 0x40 to save-buffer byte 0x8020770B after the current save flags word was read as zero. This was temporary door-access preparation, not natural progression. Project64 restored the byte to zero when all cheats were disabled. Every cheat was off before the LLL capture; no code was active during measurement.
preparation.baseline: Issue35 baseline state; 4 lives at course entry. The post-contact castle respawn HUD showed 3 lives.

inputs.note: Sign modal was visible; no movement asserted.
Last movement pulse before the lava-contact transition.

runtimeRows.note: Transition to the castle painting return position after the course-contact/death interval; do not treat as a burn-action row.

burnInterval.floorPointer: 0x801A2420 for contact and all sampled action rows through sequence 4059; area pointer 0x8033B90C, area index 1. Candidate floor-type reads later include 23151 and 0 at the same floor pointer; the cause is unknown and these late reads are not used to characterize the surface.
burnInterval.counterInterpretation: The 274 samples span 5.932 seconds of host time, not 274 simulation frames. Loop-counter pairs are equal on the trigger sample and span 112725..112891 over the interval, but repeat; the final 20 rows share 112891. The action value remained sampled during repeated counter values and the area transition, so this record does not establish a burn-action duration or 274 physics updates.
burnInterval.outcome: Course contact was followed by the numeric action above and then a castle-area respawn. HUD screenshots showed 4 lives at course entry and 3 after the respawn. No health field or health decrement was measured.

dispatcher.predicate: For floor type 1, the dispatcher calls the helper when Mario action bits 0x800 and 0x2000 are clear.

burnHelper.predicateAndEffects: Requires Mario action bit 0x10000 clear and Y < floorY + 10. If Mario flag bit 0x4 is clear, increments signed byte MarioState+0xB2 by 18 when bit 0x10 is clear, otherwise by 12; then calls FUN_802521a0 and FUN_80253178(m, 0x010208B7, 0).

exactRomCorrelation.interpretation: The captured contact has floorType 1, Y at the floor, and the exact numeric action argument used by the USA rev0 type-1 helper. The target counter at MarioState+0xB2 is not identified as health; no damage amount is claimed.

limits: This is one bounded runtime trial with external scalar sampling; counter reads bracket fields but equal pairs do not make a sample atomic.
No health field or health decrement was instrumented. The HUD life decrease is a separate observed outcome and does not establish a health value.
No symbolic action name is inferred from 0x010208B7; the exact-ROM evidence shows the helper passes that numeric action to the action setter.

Several temporary isolated save-flag fixture attempts during courtyard and basement preparation were reverted by Project64. The final successful basement-door crossing used only the reviewed one-byte 0x40 write, then all cheats were disabled before entering LLL and sampling. This is not natural progression evidence.
Raw traces, screenshots, input log, ROM, save states, and EEPROM remain local. Only selected scalar rows and hashes are included here.
